rubric.name: 像真人在讲
rubric.question: 逐句：自然 / 有点怪 / 很怪。书面腔、讲解腔、翻译腔、念稿感、报菜名式罗列都算怪

rubric.name: 衔接与过渡
rubric.question: 开场、本期内容、章节转换、举例前后：像一个人顺着思路往下讲，而不是「下面讲第一点」式的模板或目录朗读；上下句接得上

rubric.name: 一遍听懂
rubric.question: 只靠耳朵：一句只带一个新意思；指代清楚（说「这个」时观众知道指什么）；术语先解释再用；数字、同音字不会听错

rubric.name: 精炼
rubric.question: 没有废话、重复、正确的空话；删掉不影响理解的句子要指出来

rubric.name: 口吻与节奏
rubric.question: 从头到尾是同一个亲切、清楚、不端着的讲解者；长短句交替，每句适合一口气念完

rubric.name: 改写
rubric.question: 每句「有点怪 / 很怪」都给出可以直接替换、不更长的中文改写；列出最别扭的 5 句并排序

rubric.name: 复核上一轮

rubric.name: Flow and transitions

rubric.name: Clear on one hearing
rubric.question: Ear only: one new idea per line; clear reference ('this' points to something); terms explained before used; numbers and words not misheard

rubric.name: Tight
rubric.question: No filler, repetition, or empty truisms; point out lines that could go without losing anything

rubric.name: Voice and rhythm
rubric.question: One warm, clear, unpretentious narrator throughout; varied sentence length; each line sayable in one breath

items.law_name: 中文屏幕文字（PPT 式画面）
items.checks: 逐屏看画面上的中文字：是不是只列纲要、够不够简练、和口播有没有分工、看不看得完。
items.how: 硬上限（超了必须报）：标题 ≤12 字；其余每块 ≤16 字；同屏文字块 ≤4 块（不含页眉小标签、出处与图表刻度）；一屏总字数 ≤36 字。屏幕下方还有口播字幕，观众要同时看。计数口径（第 2 轮裁决定，2026-11-09）：页眉小标签、案例页签、出处、片尾署名不计；同构的列表 / 表格 / 卡片行（每项 ≤8 字、最多 6 项、样子一样）合算 1 块，编号不计字；图里的文字（区域名、曲线名、轴标题、柱条标签、图上注释）要计字数，整张图合算 1 块，只有坐标刻度数字豁免；表格的列头算在表里。
items.what: 逐屏看画面上的中文字：是不是只列纲要、够不够简练、和口播有没有分工、看不看得完。
items.problem: 上一版屏幕文字很多是整句（如「另训一个模型，在两家医院的片子上认医院的准确率——胸片里藏着医院的“指纹”」），等于把口播又印了一遍；用户要求画面只列纲要、相对简练（2026-11-08）。
items.model_why: Claude 单审：a 位评分即最终分，不对比、不裁决

rubric.name: 只列纲要
rubric.question: 每屏只放关键词、短语、关键数字、标签；不是口播整句的复述。按硬上限逐屏数字数，超了就报

rubric.name: 与口播分工
rubric.question: 屏幕给结构、数字、对比，口播负责解释；不和口播逐字重复，也不出现口播没说过的新说法；术语、叫法与口播一致

rubric.name: 层级与体例
rubric.question: 一眼先看到什么、第二眼看什么；标题—要点—注释不超过三级；编号、标签、章节名、目录项前后一致（例：目录写的和章节卡写的是不是同一个说法）

rubric.name: 中文措辞与排版
rubric.question: 短语化、不带句末句号；标点、引号、空格规范；不半中半英；**标题、章名读出来要顺**：名词堆砌、生造的名词短语（如「现实里的祸」）算必改

rubric.name: 看得完

items.checks: Screen by screen: is the on-screen English an outline (not prose), tight, divided from the narration, and readable in time?
items.how: Hard limits (report every breach): title ≤6 words; any other block ≤9 words; ≤4 text blocks per screen (not counting the small eyebrow label, source line or chart ticks); ≤22 words per screen. Narration subtitles also sit at the bottom of the frame. Counting rules (round-2 ruling, 2026-11-09): eyebrow labels, case tabs, source lines and end-card credits are exempt; a list, table or card row of look-alike items (each ≤6 words, at most 6 items) counts as one block, and numbering doesn't count as words; in-chart text (zone names, curve names, axis titles, bar labels, callouts) counts toward words and the whole chart counts as one block — only axis tick numbers are exempt; a table's column headers count with the table.
items.what: Screen by screen: is the on-screen English an outline (not prose), tight, divided from the narration, and readable in time?
items.problem: The previous version put full sentences on screen (e.g. 'A separate model identified the hospital for scans from two hospitals — a hospital fingerprint'), repeating the narration. The user wants outline-only, concise slides (2026-11-08).
items.model_why: Claude 单审：a 位评分即最终分，不对比、不裁决

rubric.name: Outline, not prose
rubric.question: Only keywords, short phrases, key numbers, labels; no full narration sentences. Count words per screen against the hard limits

rubric.name: Divided from narration
rubric.question: Screen carries structure, numbers, contrasts; narration explains. No verbatim repetition, no new claims the narration doesn't make; terms match the narration

rubric.name: Hierarchy and consistency
rubric.question: What reads first, second; ≤3 levels (title, point, note); numbering, labels, chapter names and agenda items consistent with each other

rubric.name: Native phrasing and style
rubric.question: Sentence case headline style; no Chinglish; consistent punctuation (no trailing periods on fragments), en dashes, quotes; parallel grammar in lists; **chapter titles and headings must read naturally aloud** — awkward noun stacks are must-fix

rubric.name: Readable in time
rubric.question: From the screenshot and how long it stays: readable in time (~3 words/s while also reading subtitles and the chart)

rubric.name: Rewrites
rubric.question: For every breach or awkward phrase, a shorter drop-in rewrite
